title: Claims Document Q&A for a Mid-Size P&C Insurer
business_problem: Adjusters spent 20-30 minutes per claim manually searching policy documents, prior correspondence, and inspection reports to answer coverage questions, slowing claim cycle time.
security_considerations: PII in claim narratives redacted before indexing
Row-level access control so adjusters only retrieve claims in their assigned region
All retrieved passages cited back to source document for auditability
business_outcome: Average claim research time dropped from 25 minutes to under 5 minutes per claim, with a 30% reduction in escalations for missing information.
lessons_learned: Citation-backed answers were essential to get adjuster trust, not just answer accuracy
Chunking policy documents by clause (not fixed token windows) meaningfully improved retrieval precision

title: Clinical Guideline Assistant for a Regional Hospital Network
business_problem: Clinicians needed fast, trustworthy answers to guideline and formulary questions during patient visits, without leaving the EHR workflow.
security_considerations: PHI-regulated data classification with encryption at rest and in transit
No PHI persisted in model provider logs; zero-retention API configuration
Mandatory human review before any clinical suggestion reaches a chart
business_outcome: Guideline lookup time fell by 70%, and formulary-related order errors decreased in the pilot unit over a two-quarter measurement window.
lessons_learned: Zero-retention contractual terms with the model vendor were a hard prerequisite for clinical sign-off
Clinicians preferred short, sourced answers over long generated summaries

title: KYC Policy Assistant for a Retail Bank's Onboarding Team
business_problem: Onboarding analysts referenced a constantly-changing set of KYC and AML policy documents, leading to inconsistent account-opening decisions across branches.
security_considerations: Full audit trail of every retrieved passage tied to the resulting onboarding decision
Policy index rebuilt automatically whenever compliance publishes an update, with old versions retained for audit
business_outcome: Cross-branch KYC decision consistency improved measurably, and new-analyst ramp time to policy proficiency was cut in half.
lessons_learned: Versioning the knowledge index mattered as much as the retrieval quality itself
Analysts needed a way to flag an answer as outdated, which fed back into re-indexing priority

title: Playbook-Aware Contract Research Assistant for an In-House Legal Team
business_problem: In-house counsel needed to quickly find precedent language and prior negotiated positions across thousands of historical contracts.
security_considerations: Contract corpus segmented by client/matter to prevent cross-matter leakage
Outside counsel access scoped separately from internal legal staff
business_outcome: Precedent research time dropped from hours to minutes for common clause types, freeing senior counsel for higher-judgment review.
lessons_learned: Matter-level access segmentation had to be enforced at the retrieval layer, not just the UI
Lawyers trusted the tool far more once every suggested clause linked to its source contract

title: Agentic Fraud Investigation Workflow for a National Insurer
business_problem: Fraud investigators manually cross-referenced claims, policyholder history, and external databases, a multi-system process that took days per suspicious claim.
security_considerations: Agent actions limited to read + draft-recommendation; no autonomous claim denial
Every agent step logged to an immutable audit trail for regulatory review
Human investigator approval required before any case is escalated externally
business_outcome: Time to flag high-risk claims for investigation dropped from days to hours, increasing recovered-fraud dollars per investigator.
lessons_learned: Defining clear checkpoint boundaries up front avoided scope creep into fully autonomous decisioning
Investigators wanted to see the agent's evidence trail, not just its conclusion

title: New-Hire Onboarding Orchestration Agent for a 15,000-Employee Enterprise
business_problem: Onboarding required coordinating IT provisioning, badge issuance, benefits enrollment, and manager tasks across five disconnected systems, frequently missing steps.
security_considerations: Agent scoped to provisioning workflows only, no access to compensation data
HR manager approval checkpoint before account creation for contractor roles
business_outcome: Missed onboarding steps dropped to near zero, and new-hire day-one readiness improved from 60% to over 95%.
lessons_learned: The highest-value checkpoint was approval before account creation, not after
Connecting five legacy systems took longer than building the agent logic itself

title: Supplier Exception Handling Agent for a Global Manufacturer
business_problem: Procurement analysts manually resolved purchase-order mismatches (price, quantity, delivery date) against supplier invoices, a high-volume repetitive task prone to backlog.
security_considerations: Agent cannot approve payments; only drafts a resolution for finance sign-off
Full ERP write access logged and reviewed weekly
business_outcome: Invoice exception backlog fell by 65%, and average resolution time dropped from 4 days to under 8 hours.
lessons_learned: Currency and unit normalization across supplier formats was the single biggest source of false-positive mismatches
Giving the agent a 'propose, don't post' boundary made finance stakeholders comfortable approving the rollout

title: Tier-2 Network Incident Triage Agent for a Telecom Operator
business_problem: Tier-2 support engineers spent significant time correlating alarms across monitoring systems before even starting root-cause diagnosis.
security_considerations: Agent restricted to read-only access on production network telemetry
All proposed remediation steps require on-call engineer approval before execution
business_outcome: Mean time to root-cause identification improved by roughly 40% during the pilot on core network incidents.
lessons_learned: Read-only scoping for the agent was non-negotiable for the network operations team
Posting agent findings directly into the existing Slack incident channel drove adoption more than a separate UI

title: Real-Time Customer Support Copilot for an E-commerce Retailer
business_problem: Support agents needed to look up order status, return policy, and product details across multiple systems mid-conversation, extending average handle time.
security_considerations: Copilot suggestions require agent confirmation before sending to a customer
Payment details masked in any context passed to the model
business_outcome: Average handle time dropped 22% and first-contact resolution improved, with no increase in customer complaint rate.
lessons_learned: Sub-second suggestion latency was necessary for agents to actually use the tool mid-call
Agents ignored suggestions that didn't match the brand's tone, so tone-tuning the prompt mattered more than raw accuracy

title: Relationship Manager Copilot for Wealth Management
business_problem: Relationship managers needed real-time talking points and portfolio context pulled up during live client calls without breaking conversation flow.
security_considerations: Suggestions never sent directly to the client; advisor-facing only
Portfolio data scoped to the advisor's assigned client list
business_outcome: Advisors reported meaningfully higher confidence in cross-sell conversations, with a measurable increase in follow-on meeting bookings.
lessons_learned: Keeping the sidecar strictly advisor-facing (never client-facing) simplified compliance review significantly
Advisors wanted the copilot to surface caveats, not just opportunities

title: Booking Agent Copilot for a Travel & Hospitality Contact Center
business_problem: Booking agents juggled fare rules, loyalty status, and change-fee policies across systems while customers waited on the line.
security_considerations: No autonomous rebooking; copilot only surfaces options for the agent to execute
Loyalty tier and payment data excluded from prompt context by default
business_outcome: Average call time decreased and policy-exception errors (wrong fee waived, wrong fare rule applied) dropped substantially.
lessons_learned: Fare-rule content changed often enough that a stale cache became the main failure mode, requiring a shorter refresh interval
Agents most valued the copilot for exceptions, not for routine bookings they already knew well

title: IT Service Desk Copilot for a Global Professional Services Firm
business_problem: Level-1 IT support handled a high volume of repetitive password, access, and software-install requests, creating long queue times for more complex issues.
security_considerations: Identity verification required before any account-related suggestion is actioned
Copilot cannot reset credentials directly; hands off to the identity API under agent supervision
business_outcome: Level-1 ticket resolution time dropped by half, and queue backlog for complex issues shrank accordingly.
lessons_learned: Tight integration with the identity/access API was more valuable than broader knowledge coverage
A narrow, well-scoped copilot outperformed an earlier broad 'ask IT anything' prototype

title: Automated Submission Triage for Commercial Underwriting
business_problem: Underwriters manually reviewed every inbound submission to classify risk category and completeness before detailed review, creating a queue bottleneck.
security_considerations: Classification pipeline runs in an isolated batch environment with no external network egress
Incomplete-data flags reviewed by a human before any submission is declined
business_outcome: Submission triage throughput increased roughly 4x, letting underwriters focus review time on complex, high-value accounts.
lessons_learned: Batch classification worked well precisely because no single decision needed to be real-time
Clear escalation rules for low-confidence classifications prevented silent misrouting

title: Product Review Moderation and Tagging Pipeline for a Marketplace
business_problem: Millions of monthly product reviews needed moderation for policy violations and tagging by sentiment and topic, far beyond manual review capacity.
security_considerations: Automated removal limited to high-confidence policy violations; borderline cases queued for human moderators
Image and text moderation logs retained for a fixed period to support appeals
business_outcome: Moderation coverage reached effectively 100% of submitted reviews, cutting median policy-violation exposure time from days to minutes.
lessons_learned: A conservative auto-removal confidence threshold reduced false positives that had previously frustrated sellers
Appeals volume dropped once moderation reasons were shown to the reviewer

title: Pipeline Inspection Image Classification for an Energy Utility
business_problem: Drone inspection footage of pipeline infrastructure required manual review to flag corrosion and defects, a slow process against a large and growing backlog of footage.
security_considerations: Inspection imagery classified as critical-infrastructure data with restricted access
Every flagged defect routed to a certified inspector for confirmation before work orders are issued
business_outcome: Backlog of unreviewed footage was cleared within a quarter, and flagged-defect turnaround time dropped from weeks to days.
lessons_learned: Model performance varied significantly by camera angle and lighting, requiring a targeted fine-tuning pass on utility-specific footage
The batch pipeline's value was throughput, not novel detection accuracy over the existing manual process

title: Overnight Shipment Exception Classification for a Logistics Provider
business_problem: Thousands of nightly shipment exceptions (delays, address issues, customs holds) needed categorization each morning before regional teams could act on them.
security_considerations: Customs-related exception data handled under the same controls as cross-border compliance records
Pipeline outputs validated against a sample audit each morning before regional dispatch
business_outcome: Morning triage time for regional operations teams dropped from roughly two hours to fifteen minutes.
lessons_learned: Running the pipeline overnight avoided any real-time latency requirement entirely, simplifying the architecture
A small daily human audit sample caught drift in exception categories before it became a systemic issue

title: Adverse Event Report Triage for a Pharmaceutical Manufacturer
business_problem: Pharmacovigilance teams manually screened incoming adverse event reports for severity and regulatory reportability, a compliance-critical bottleneck as report volume grew.
security_considerations: PHI redaction applied before any report leaves the validated processing boundary
Every automated severity classification independently reviewed by a qualified person, per regulatory requirement
business_outcome: Initial triage time per report fell significantly, helping the team consistently meet regulatory reporting-window deadlines.
lessons_learned: Regulatory requirements meant the model could accelerate triage but never replace the qualified-person review step
Validation documentation for the pipeline took longer to produce than the pipeline itself

title: Multi-Agent Production Planning for a Global Electronics Manufacturer
business_problem: Production planning required continuously reconciling demand forecasts, supplier lead times, and factory capacity across regions, a coordination problem too complex for a single automated workflow.
security_considerations: Each sub-agent scoped to a single system's write permissions, no shared over-privileged credential
Orchestrator changes to production schedules require a planning-manager checkpoint above a defined cost threshold
business_outcome: Planning cycle time dropped from days to hours, and forecast-to-plan variance improved across the pilot product lines.
lessons_learned: Per-agent credential scoping was the single most important control for stakeholder trust
Coordination failures were easier to debug once each sub-agent's reasoning was logged separately rather than as one combined trace

title: Autonomous Research Desk for Equity Research Analysts
business_problem: Analysts spent significant time assembling company research packets from earnings calls, filings, and market data before starting actual analysis.
security_considerations: Research agents restricted to approved public and licensed data sources only, no open web access
Every claim in the final packet must trace to a cited source before it reaches an analyst
business_outcome: Time to assemble a first-draft research packet dropped from a full day to under two hours, per analyst feedback in the pilot group.
lessons_learned: Restricting agents to a licensed data source allowlist avoided a major compliance concern early in the design
Analysts still fully rewrote conclusions, but reused the assembled facts and citations directly

title: Self-Healing Network Operations for a Telecom Core Network
business_problem: Routine network remediation (capacity rebalancing, known-fault recovery) required manual coordination across multiple operations teams, delaying resolution for well-understood issues.
security_considerations: Autonomous remediation limited to a pre-approved playbook of low-risk actions; anything outside the playbook requires human approval
Full action log streamed to the network operations center in real time for oversight
business_outcome: Mean time to resolution for known-pattern incidents dropped substantially, freeing engineers to focus on novel issues.
lessons_learned: Starting with a narrow, pre-approved playbook was what made an autonomous rollout acceptable to network operations leadership
Real-time visibility into agent actions mattered more to stakeholders than the autonomy itself

title: Citizen Services Knowledge Assistant for a State Government Agency
business_problem: Call center staff struggled to keep up with frequently changing benefits eligibility rules spread across dozens of policy documents.
security_considerations: Deployment within a FedRAMP-authorized environment boundary
No citizen PII included in any prompt; lookups keyed by case ID resolved server-side
business_outcome: Call handling time for eligibility questions decreased, and policy-application consistency across call center staff improved.
lessons_learned: FedRAMP authorization requirements shaped the deployment topology more than any modeling decision
Staff needed plain-language answers with a link to the exact regulation, not regulation text verbatim

title: Academic Advising Copilot for a Large Public University
business_problem: Academic advisors managed large student caseloads and needed fast access to degree requirements and prior advising notes during walk-in sessions.
security_considerations: Student record access scoped under FERPA to the advisor's assigned caseload only
Advising notes summarized for the advisor's own review, never sent to the student directly
business_outcome: Average walk-in advising session prep time dropped substantially, letting advisors see more students during peak registration periods.
lessons_learned: FERPA scoping requirements were simplest to enforce at the data-access layer rather than in the prompt
Advisors valued a concise session-prep summary far more than an open-ended chat interface

title: Automated Content Tagging Pipeline for a Streaming Media Library
business_problem: A growing content library needed consistent metadata tagging (genre, mood, content warnings) for search and recommendation, far beyond the manual cataloging team's capacity.
security_considerations: Content-warning classifications reviewed by the catalog team before publishing to the live library
Pipeline runs against a staging copy of the content library, never production streaming infrastructure directly
business_outcome: Tagging throughput increased roughly 6x, letting the catalog team clear a multi-year backlog within a single quarter.
lessons_learned: Multimodal classification of both video and audio track content was needed to catch content-warning cases text metadata alone missed
A lightweight human spot-check step caught genre miscategorizations that materially affected recommendations

title: Technician Diagnostic Copilot for an Automotive Service Network
business_problem: Service technicians needed fast access to model-specific diagnostic procedures and technical service bulletins while working on a vehicle in the bay.
security_considerations: Diagnostic suggestions clearly labeled as advisory; technician retains final sign-off on any repair
Vehicle identification data scoped to the active service order only
business_outcome: Average diagnostic time for complex issues decreased, and first-time-fix rate improved across pilot service centers.
lessons_learned: Technicians most valued fast access to the exact technical service bulletin over general troubleshooting advice
Photo-based query support (technician photographs a component) drove adoption more than text search alone

title: Storm Outage Response Coordination Agent for an Electric Utility
business_problem: During major storm events, dispatch coordinators manually triaged thousands of outage reports and crew assignments under severe time pressure.
security_considerations: Agent proposes crew assignments; dispatch supervisor retains final approval at all times
System designed to degrade gracefully to fully manual dispatch if the agent's confidence drops during extreme load
business_outcome: Average outage-to-crew-dispatch time improved during the storm season pilot, most notably during peak-volume events.
lessons_learned: Graceful degradation to manual mode under extreme load was as important a design requirement as the automation itself
Dispatch coordinators wanted priority reasoning shown up front, not buried in a detail view

title: Autonomous Inventory Rebalancing Across a Regional Store Network
business_problem: Regional inventory managers manually decided which stores should transfer stock to which, a decision that scaled poorly across hundreds of stores and thousands of SKUs.
security_considerations: Transfer-order agent capped to a pre-approved dollar threshold per transaction; larger transfers require manager approval
All automated transfer decisions logged with the demand signal that triggered them, for post-hoc audit
business_outcome: Stockout rate for high-velocity SKUs declined, and manual rebalancing workload for regional managers dropped substantially.
lessons_learned: A hard dollar cap on autonomous transfer decisions was what got the finance team comfortable with the rollout
Regional managers needed an easy override, not just a dashboard, to keep trust in the system during edge cases

title: Agent Support Assistant for Independent Insurance Agents
business_problem: Independent agents selling multiple carriers' products needed fast, accurate answers about product coverage differences without calling underwriting.
security_considerations: Product guidance clearly disclaimed as informational, not binding coverage confirmation
Underwriting escalation path preserved for any question outside the copilot's confidence threshold
business_outcome: Underwriting call volume for routine product questions dropped meaningfully, and agent quote turnaround time improved.
lessons_learned: A visible confidence threshold with an escalation path avoided the copilot overstating coverage guarantees
Agents adopted the tool fastest when it was embedded directly in their existing quoting software

title: Visual Defect Classification on a Consumer Electronics Line
business_problem: Quality inspectors manually reviewed sampled product images for surface defects, limiting inspection coverage to a small percentage of total production.
security_considerations: Inspection pipeline isolated on the factory network with no external connectivity
Borderline defect classifications routed to a human inspector rather than auto-rejected
business_outcome: Inspection coverage increased from roughly 10% to effectively 100% of units, catching defects earlier in the line.
lessons_learned: Line lighting variability required more image normalization work than the classification model itself
100% coverage surfaced upstream process issues that sampling had never revealed
